## Status and principal claim

This is a conditional research derivation, not an externally reviewed paper or a claim of established priority. Its algorithmic conclusions import the homogeneous log-concave coefficient FPRAS in Chen and Liu, arXiv:2610.06724v1, Theorem 5.1 and its every-execution rational implementation in Remark A.4. The counting theorem has not been independently certified in full, and neither its FPRAS nor the reversible quantum compiler has been implemented in this run. The included code tests finite identities and small numerical instances, not the full algorithms.

The principal new candidate contribution is an explicit passage from positive local imaginary-time dynamics to **entrywise relative approximation**, and from there to coherent state access and relative replica contraction. Relative accuracy matters: a small trace-distance perturbation alone does not protect an exponentially small purity or the normalization of a rare conditioned state.

The main spin family, in a specified computational basis, is

$$
 H=\frac12\sum_{e=uv}\bigl[d_e Z_uZ_v-f_e(X_uX_v+Y_uY_v)\bigr]
       +\sum_i h_iZ_i,\qquad f_e\geq |d_e|,
 \tag{1}
$$

with rational coefficients on an arbitrary finite graph. Zero edges can be deleted. The longitudinal fields $h_i$ may have either sign. The inequalities are edgewise; no bounded-degree, geometric-locality, high-temperature, area-law, or physical-mixing promise is made.

Set

$$
 V=\sum_e(f_e+\max(d_e,0))+2\sum_i|h_i|.
 \tag{2}
$$

**Conditional theorem.** For the input (1), rational $\beta>0$, accuracy $0<\epsilon<1/2$, and failure probability $0<\delta<1/2$, there are algorithms with the following guarantees, assuming the imported coefficient FPRAS.

* A randomized classical compiler produces a quantum circuit preparing an $\epsilon$-approximation in trace distance to the canonical purification of $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}$. # Resumable research state: positive kernels / replica access
Date: 2026-10-07. Local checkpoint, not a GitHub commit.

## Start here
Read `proofs/relative_kernels_and_replica_access.md` (same content as the PDF), then `RESULT_CARDS.json`, `FAILED_ROUTES.md`, and `checks/results.json`.
The strongest current candidate is **conditional relative replica access for thermal states, gapped-sector ground states, and normalized global ground-space projectors of easy-plane XXZ systems**, obtained via a new positive-word entrywise-relative product bound. Do not describe it as certified, priority-cleared, practical hardware, or first ground-state preparation.

## Load-bearing imported capital
Chen--Liu arXiv:2610.06724v1 Theorem 5.1 + Remark A.4: homogeneous multiaffine nonnegative log-concave complementary-degree coefficient FPRAS, rational oracles, support witnesses, coefficient ranges, every-execution time cap. Base cost O(M^10 B^2 eta^-2 log^2(2B/eta)); amplify logarithmically. Entire theorem not independently certified or implemented here.
Astra N63: weighted-prefix randomized coherent compiler, not exponentially good tapes. Source proof partially retrieved far enough to read this lemma and acquired interfaces. N57 checked to exclude a misleading PEPS/acquisition overlap.

## Main acquired physical interface
H = (1/2) sum_e [d_e ZZ - f_e(XX+YY)] + sum_i h_i Z,
f_e >= |d_e|, all rational, arbitrary graph and signed longitudinal fields.
A=cI-H=sum nonnegative local A_j,
c=sum |d_e|/2+sum|h_i|,
V=sum(f_e+max(d_e,0))+2sum|h_i| bounds sum local norms.
Edge A has outer diagonal d_-; middle diagonal d_+; exchange f.
Identity-plus-step gate weights a=1+t d_-, b=1+t d_+, c=tf satisfy linear triangles at sufficiently small t. Field gate gives a positive linear two-port polynomial.
Bipartite antiferromagnetic XXZ is mapped by Z on one sublattice. Isotropic bipartite Heisenberg and zero-field EPR (the latter after uniform local Clifford change) are covered. Do not claim arbitrary EPR-basis fields are covered.

## New analytic mechanism
For nonnegative A=sum A_j, kernel K=e^(tau A), lower bound lambda on all nonzero entries:
C=[product_j(I+tau A_j/m)]^m satisfies (1-alpha)K <= C <= (1+alpha)K ENTRYWISE.
Choose B0 with 2^-B0 <=lambda, k0>=max(1,ceil(6 tau V), B0+ceil log2(64/alpha)), m>=max(2k0,ceil(8k0^2/alpha)).
Proof: coefficient of each length-k word has embedding count bet
